description: Create a pin authored by Pincushion AI. ONLY call this from the pincushion-critic subagent, /critique-latest-deploy, or an explicitly requested Pincushion Crit command such as Grok Build /pincushion-crit (including the confirmed first Crit during /pincushion setup) — never from an ordinary coding prompt, since the bot voice is reserved for AI-driven UI/copy/a11y and product-experience feedback (flows, empty/error states, terminology, trust). Each call should produce one tasteful, high-signal pin (max 3 per page in a critique run). The body must be concrete and actionable: name the specific element + the specific problem + the suggested fix in <40 words (up to 55 for a flow critique that must name the step before/after). Forbidden: layout philosophy, business-model commentary, roadmap ideation (a missing affordance at a specific element IS in scope), generic "consider improving hierarchy" advice. Always read the project's critique context (`ai.critique.effectiveContext` from get_project_context — falls back to `brandContext` when no compiled brief exists) before drafting the body so the critique is on-brand. If `ai.critique.staleness` is "stale" or "missing", suggest the user run /refresh-brand before continuing. Repeating the same semantic finding on the same route and selector with only query values changed returns `duplicate_variant`; inspect a distinct state, scenario, or element instead.

body.description: The critique itself. Concrete + actionable, <40 words, names the element and proposes a fix. This becomes the first thread message on the pin.

componentName.description: Optional component name (e.g. LWC component, React component) for grouping. Used by get_component_feedback.

critiqueRunId.description: Required stable ID for this Crit run. Reuse the exact same value for every pin in the run; Pincushion stores it as critique-run:<id> and verifies it before a Crit report can be minted.

operationId.description: Optional opaque idempotency ID. When a response is pending_reconciliation, retry the same submission with the returned operationId; use a new ID for an intentionally separate pin.

pageTitle.description: Optional page title for the .feedback file header. Defaults to pageUrl if omitted.

pageUrl.description: Full URL of the page being critiqued (e.g. "http://localhost:3000/dashboard").

projectId.description: Project ID to associate the pin with. Defaults to the MCP server's configured project.

selector.description: CSS selector for the element the critique targets. The Chrome extension uses this to position the pin since the bot has no live page coords. Be specific (e.g. 'main button[type="submit"]' not just 'button').

severity.description: "high" = ships-blocking (broken contrast, broken keyboard nav, misleading CTA copy, a workflow dead-end in a core flow). "medium" = worth-fixing (minor copy issues, cramped spacing, terminology drift, polish opportunities). 'low' is intentionally not allowed — bot pins must be worth acting on.

tags.description: Optional tags. "pincushion-ai" is added automatically. Add domain tags like "a11y", "copy", "flow", "empty-state", "terminology", "deploy:<hash>" for traceability.

visibility.description: Use project_members for findings on signed-in app screens.
